While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to Slovenian legal entities registered in ESA-STAR, as prime tenderer and foresees the following standard activity types:Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participation in ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use on futureESA missions or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 1 and the target TRL shall be TRL 3 or below. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 150,000.Type B Flight- and Ground Segment-related Research and Development Activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 3 and the target TRL shall be TRL 5. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 400 000 (flight related)/EUR 300 000 (ground related).Type C Flight Opportunities for mature existing Slovenian technologies or products in collaboration with experienced European players, to be involved in non-ESA mission in order to become flight proven. The start TRL shall be at least 5 and the target TRL shall be TRL 9. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 750 000 (inc. launch and operation cost). The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity. Maximum 20% of the budget may be assigned tonon-Slovenian entities, however launch and integration tasks are excluded from this limitation.Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 100,000.Type F Space Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity.Type G1 University courses/modules leading to a qualification (BSc or MSc) in space related topics that correspond to the needs of national space industry and to encourage career in spaceandanswer to national space industry needs. Details Unlocking Space for Business The UK Space Agency’s Unlocking Space for Business (USB) programme is seeking to accelerate the adoption of space-enabled data and services to address environmental intelligence and emissions challenges across the UK economy. This challenge-led competition is designed to support projects that demonstrate how space-enabled data, technologies and services can help organisations improve environmental monitoring, emissions measurement, reporting and verification, and wider environmental decision-making. The competition aims to stimulate greater collaboration between end users, data integrators and space-sector suppliers, while supporting the development of solutions with credible pathways to future operational adoption. Who can apply This competition is open to UK-registered end-user businesses, including SMEs, leading a consortium with at least one UK space supplier and any additional integrator or delivery partner organisations required to support project delivery. For the purposes of this competition, end-user businesses are organisations that use space-enabled products, services or insights to address operational challenges, improve decision-making, manage risk or deliver commercial outcomes. The competition is particularly aimed at end-user organisations operating in sectors including financial services, insurance, asset management, energy, utilities, infrastructure, agriculture, land management and environmental services. Applications from organisations in other sectors are also welcome, provided they can demonstrate a clear environmental intelligence or emissions-related use case aligned with the competition objectives. The UK Space Agency invites applications from end-user-led consortia comprising: An end-user organisation seeking to address one of the competition’s environmental intelligence or emissions challenge statements At least one supplier of space-enabled data, products or services; and Any additional delivery partners or integrators required to support successful project delivery. Applicant webinar The UK Space Agency will host an applicant webinar on 3 November 2026, 11:00 GMT to provide an overview of the competition, explain the challenge statements, outline the application process and answer participant questions. Interested organisations are strongly encouraged to attend. Details of how to register can be found Unlocking Space for Business: Environmental Intelligence and Emissions Grant Call Briefing Webinar. Funding available The UK Space Agency intends to award up to £2 million through this competition. Applicants may request up to £400,000 grant funding per project. Total project costs may be higher where match funding is provided by consortium partners. In exceptional circumstances, the UK Space Agency reserves the right to adjust the total funding available, the number of projects funded, or the value of individual awards. Project duration Projects are expected to start in January 2027 and run for approximately 9 months. Projects must be sufficiently mature to demonstrate operational value within the funded period and deliver measurable outcomes by the end of the project. How to apply Applications must be submitted through the Flexigrant portal by 16:00 GMT on 11 December 2026. Applicants must complete all required sections of the online application form and upload the required supporting documentation through the Flexigrant platform which can be accessed here: Flexigrant . Applications submitted by email will not be accepted. Late applications will not be accepted. Your application must include: A completed application form; Annex A: Proposed Milestone Table Annex B: Project Cost Breakdown Annex C: National Security Questionnaire (where required) Any additional supporting documentation requested within the application process. Applicants should read the full competition guidance before submitting an application. Sign up for emails or print this page Get emails about this page Print this page

Details Unlocking Space for Business The UK Space Agency’s Unlocking Space for Business (USB) programme is seeking to accelerate the adoption of space-enabled data and services to address environmental intelligence and emissions challenges across the UK economy. This challenge-led competition is designed to support projects that demonstrate how space-enabled data, technologies and services can help organisations improve environmental monitoring, emissions measurement, reporting and verification, and wider environmental decision-making. The competition aims to stimulate greater collaboration between end users, data integrators and space-sector suppliers, while supporting the development of solutions with credible pathways to future operational adoption. Who can apply This competition is open to UK-registered end-user businesses, including SMEs, leading a consortium with at least one UK space supplier and any additional integrator or delivery partner organisations required to support project delivery. For the purposes of this competition, end-user businesses are organisations that use space-enabled products, services or insights to address operational challenges, improve decision-making, manage risk or deliver commercial outcomes. The competition is particularly aimed at end-user organisations operating in sectors including financial services, insurance, asset management, energy, utilities, infrastructure, agriculture, land management and environmental services. Applications from organisations in other sectors are also welcome, provided they can demonstrate a clear environmental intelligence or emissions-related use case aligned with the competition objectives. The UK Space Agency invites applications from end-user-led consortia comprising: An end-user organisation seeking to address one of the competition’s environmental intelligence or emissions challenge statements At least one supplier of space-enabled data, products or services; and Any additional delivery partners or integrators required to support successful project delivery. Applicant webinar On 3 November 2026, the UK Space Agency hosted a briefing webinar to provide prospective applicants with further information about the competition. A recording of the webinar can be accessed here: Unlocking Space for Business Environmental Intelligence and Emissions Grant Call Webinar - YouTube, and the information presented during the session is included in the annex to this page. The webinar also provided an opportunity for prospective applicants to submit questions. Relevant questions and responses have subsequently been incorporated into the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) section in the guidance page Unlocking Space for Business: Environmental Intelligence and Emissions Grant Call - GOV.UK Funding available The UK Space Agency intends to award up to £2 million through this competition. Applicants may request up to £400,000 grant funding per project. Total project costs may be higher where match funding is provided by consortium partners. In exceptional circumstances, the UK Space Agency reserves the right to adjust the total funding available, the number of projects funded, or the value of individual awards. Project duration Projects are expected to start in January 2027 and run for approximately 9 months. Projects must be sufficiently mature to demonstrate operational value within the funded period and deliver measurable outcomes by the end of the project. How to apply Applications must be submitted through the Flexigrant portal by 16:00 GMT on 11 December 2026. Applicants must complete all required sections of the online application form and upload the required supporting documentation through the Flexigrant platform which can be accessed here: Flexigrant . Applications submitted by email will not be accepted. Late applications will not be accepted. Your application must include: A completed application form; Annex A: Proposed Milestone Table Annex B: Project Cost Breakdown Annex C: National Security Questionnaire Annex D: Details of Previous Grants for Subsidy Control Purposes (if required) Any additional supporting documentation requested within the application process. Applicants should read the full competition guidance before submitting an application. beneficiaryAdministration:
Programme Scope

This Programme supports the contracting of External Service Providers to help beneficiaries design/upscale/commercialise space-enabled green solutions or adopt commercially available ones, contributing to the transition towards more sustainable and circular business innovation practices, processes, and partnerships.

This Open Call targets applicants who are interested in using downstream space data to create solutions that have a positive environmental impact, either: for the company itself (e.g., by improving current processes to minimize resources, waste, pollution, etc.) – Type A Transformation Project or for its users (e.g., by creating new or improving existing products for better resource management, environmental monitoring, etc.) – Type B Transformation Project

Applicants should demonstrate their potential to leverage downstream space data, such as Earth Observation (EO), remote sensing, satellite navigation, etc. The program places a particular focus on supporting solutions in areas such as:

  1. Improvement of circularity in terms of improved use of resources and waste management
  2. Safe, resource-efficient, and environmentally friendly management of primary, secondary, and critical raw materials
  3. Improved environmental monitoring

Max. Grant Amount

Each selected beneficiary can receive up to 50,000 EUR to implement its project, based on the budget information indicated in the application form and paid out after successful completion and verification of results.

How to apply

Applications must be submitted via our online portal https://opportunities.getonepass.eu/opportunities/financial-support-program/2nd-open-call within the indicated deadline.

Who can apply

Single entities applying as: Self-employed individuals, Micro Enterprises, Small Enterprises, Medium-sized Enterprises, including start-ups and scale-ups.

At the time of application, these single entities should be legally registered in any EU Member State and its Overseas Countries and Territories (OCT) or Horizon Europe Associated Countries.

Number of grants available

We aim to support approximately 22 Projects in this Open Call. In particular, we aim to support approximately 6 projects requesting a scale-up voucher (i.e. up to 50.000 EUR) and 16 projects requesting an ideation/ commercialization voucher (i.e. up to 25.000 EUR). This number may vary, depending on the different types of projects to be funded and the actual requested budget.

The total budget available for this Open Call is 694 520,00 EUR. The budget may increase during the application period. In such an event, the Guide for Applicants will be updated accordingly.

The final number of awarded projects is determined by the total budget allocated to this Open Call and the overall quality of the selected projects.

Evaluation process

We will evaluate only complete proposals that are submitted via our official application platform within the indicated deadline.

The evaluation process consists of the following steps:

  1. Step 1 will check the proposals against eligibility criteria.
  2. Step 2 (if necessary) will perform a pre-scoring process.
  3. Step 3 will involve experts’ evaluation to assess the proposal according to the criteria.
  4. Step 4 when the Selection Committee will decide the “provisional list of FSTP recipients” during the Consensus Meeting
  5. Step 5 will include the legal screening of the pre-selected entities before they are invited to sign the Sub-Grant Agreement.

Download the Application Package below to apply to ESA BIC Andalusia Download the Application Package (.zip)Who Can ApplyEnsure your startup can join our incubation programme To be eligible for ESA BIC Andalusia, your startup or business idea must meet the following criteria: Space-Related InnovationYour business must have a solid connection to space-related technology, expertise, or applications. This connection can be categorized as either Downstream or Upstream: Downstream This involves the application or exploitation of space systems or technologies in non-space domains. Your business idea may focus on: Applications utilizing satellite navigation, earth observation, or satellite communication.Technology transfer involving space-related hardware, software, or intellectual property.Providing solutions that leverage space data or technology to innovate in other sectorsUpstream This relates to the development of new technologies intended for use within the space sector. Examples include: Developing new systems, subsystems, or components for space missions.Technologies and services designed for use on space missions or in human spaceflight activities.Your application must clearly justify the space connection, demonstrating how it advances or innovates within the space sector. It is crucial that the space connection is clear and justified in your application. For further guidance on ensuring your idea meets the necessary criteria, please consult the Space Connection Assessment document. This will help you evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea to meet the requirements set by ESA BIC Andalusia. Viable Business PlanYou must present a clear and viable business plan outlining your strategy for growth, the market potential of your product or service, and how your space-related innovation will be commercialized. The business plan should also detail financial projections, key milestones, and risk management strategies. Company AgeNew or existing companies less than 5 years old. If Your Company is Already Established Your startup must be legally registered in Spain and must not be older than five years at the time of application. If Your Company is Not Yet Established You are eligible to apply as an informal group of entrepreneurs, provided you commit to legally registering your startup in Andalusia upon acceptance into the programme. Company LocationYour business must be, or commit to being, located in Andalusia during the incubation period. ESA BIC Andalusia is strategically located in the Naves de Renfe building in the San Jerónimo district of Seville, near the Spanish Space Agency headquarters. Commitment to the programmeYour team must be fully committed to engaging with the ESA BIC Andalusia programme throughout the entire incubation period. This includes regular attendance at workshops, mentoring sessions, and events organized by the incubator, as well as making full use of the resources provided. How to ApplyFollow these steps and turn your ideas into successful businesses Check Your EligibilityEnsure your startup meets the eligibility criteria for ESA BIC Andalusia. If you are unsure, visit the Who can apply section for more information. Contact Our TeamIt is highly recommended to contact ESA BIC Andalusia in advance to inform us about your intention to apply. The team will assist you in determining whether your business idea is suitable for incubation and will explain what is needed from the applicant. Download The Application FormsThe Open Call for Proposals is OPEN. All application forms and supporting documents are available below. Download the full Application Package and submit your proposal. record.description: ApplyESA BIC Andalusia2026-10-29T15:23:31+01:00 Who Can ApplyEnsure your startup can join our incubation programme To be eligible for ESA BIC Andalusia, your startup or business idea must meet the following criteria: Space-Related InnovationYour business must have a solid connection to space-related technology, expertise, or applications. This connection can be categorized as either Downstream or Upstream: Downstream This involves the application or exploitation of space systems or technologies in non-space domains. Your business idea may focus on: Applications utilizing satellite navigation, earth observation, or satellite communication.Technology transfer involving space-related hardware, software, or intellectual property.Providing solutions that leverage space data or technology to innovate in other sectorsUpstream This relates to the development of new technologies intended for use within the space sector. Examples include: Developing new systems, subsystems, or components for space missions.Technologies and services designed for use on space missions or in human spaceflight activities.Your application must clearly justify the space connection, demonstrating how it advances or innovates within the space sector. It is crucial that the space connection is clear and justified in your application. For further guidance on ensuring your idea meets the necessary criteria, please consult the Space Connection Assessment document. This will help you evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea to meet the requirements set by ESA BIC Andalusia. Viable Business PlanYou must present a clear and viable business plan outlining your strategy for growth, the market potential of your product or service, and how your space-related innovation will be commercialized. The business plan should also detail financial projections, key milestones, and risk management strategies. Company AgeNew or existing companies less than 5 years old. If Your Company is Already Established Your startup must be legally registered in Spain and must not be older than five years at the time of application. If Your Company is Not Yet Established You are eligible to apply as an informal group of entrepreneurs, provided you commit to legally registering your startup in Andalusia upon acceptance into the programme. Company LocationYour business must be, or commit to being, located in Andalusia during the incubation period. ESA BIC Andalusia is strategically located in the Naves de Renfe building in the San Jerónimo district of Seville, near the Spanish Space Agency headquarters. Commitment to the programmeYour team must be fully committed to engaging with the ESA BIC Andalusia programme throughout the entire incubation period. This includes regular attendance at workshops, mentoring sessions, and events organized by the incubator, as well as making full use of the resources provided. How to ApplyFollow these steps and turn your ideas into successful businesses Check Your EligibilityEnsure your startup meets the eligibility criteria for ESA BIC Andalusia. If you are unsure, visit the Who can apply section for more information. Contact Our TeamIt is highly recommended to contact ESA BIC Andalusia in advance to inform us about your intention to apply. The team will assist you in determining whether your business idea is suitable for incubation and will explain what is needed from the applicant. Download The Application FormsAll application forms and supporting documents are available below. Download the full Application Package and submit your proposal. Download the Application Package (.zip)Prepare Your ApplicationBefore you begin filling out any forms, it is strongly recommended that you carefully read all the provided documents. Application Templates The Application Package contains the following documents: ESA BIC Andalusia Open Call (call conditions and process) ESA BIC Application Form (the document to complete and submit, including its annexes) Draft Incubation Contract Space Connection Assessment Supporting Documents Make sure to thoroughly review all supporting documents, particularly the Draft Incubation Contract. This document is crucial for understanding your contractual obligations and ensuring you are fully informed before proceeding with your application. Documents Preparation Application Form: complete all required sections following the instructions inside the form. It replaces the previous separate templates (cover letter, business plan and incubation proposal). Include details on how you intend to use the incentive funding. The form must be signed by the majority shareholder, or by shareholders jointly holding more than 50% of the shares; the signature also confirms acceptance of the Incubation Contract conditions. Draft Incubation Contract: read it carefully before applying. Modifications or amendments may only be considered in exceptional cases. Space Connection Assessment: use this document to evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea. Application SubmissionBefore submitting, review all your documents carefully. Ensure that each section is completed according to the instructions provided in the templates. eligibility.text: ASAP & Digitaler Zwilling Österreich 2026 Die Ausschreibung 2026 im Thema Weltraum & Digitalisierung Das Österreichische Weltraumprogramm ASAP und die Initiative Digitaler Zwilling Österreich bieten mit der Ausschreibung 2026 breite Möglichkeiten für Projekte in den Themen Erdbeobachtung, Navigation und Telekommunikation, Technologien für die Raumfahrt sowie Weltraumwissenschaften und Exploration. Insgesamt steht ein Budget von ca. 13 Mio. EUR zur Verfügung. Jetzt einreichen Hinweis: Bitte lesen Sie vor der Einreichung alle Informationen auf dieser Seite aufmerksam durch. Was wird gefördert? Im Fokus der Förderung stehen F&E-Projekte an der Schnittstelle zwischen Weltraum und Digitalen Technologien, zur Anwendung von Satellitendaten, Produktentwicklung für die Raumfahrt mit Hebelwirkung in die ESA, EU und globale institutionelle und kommerzielle Märkte sowie die Beteiligungen an Weltraummissionen. Wer wird gefördert? Antragsberechtigt sind Universitäten, Forschungseinrichtungen, KMU, Industrieunternehmen, Bedarfsträger und sonstige Organisationen. Wie hoch ist die Förderung? Die Förderhöhe richtet sich nach dem eingereichten Förderinstrument und der Organisationsart zwischen 35-100% der Projektkosten. Was sind die Einreichkriterien? Siehe Ausschreibungs- und Instrumentenleitfäden Wie erfolgt die Einreichung? Die Einreichung erfolgt über das eCall-System der FFG, in dem der Projektinhalt und die –kosten dargestellt werden. Welche Dokumente für die Einreichung erforderlich sein werden, wird im Ausschreibungsleitfaden angeführt. Wann gibt es eine Entscheidung? Die Förderentscheidung ist für April 2027 geplant. record.description: ASAP & Digitaler Zwilling Österreich 2026 Die Ausschreibung 2026 im Thema Weltraum & Digitalisierung Das Österreichische Weltraumprogramm ASAP und die Initiative Digitaler Zwilling Österreich bieten mit der Ausschreibung 2026 breite Möglichkeiten für Projekte in den Themen Erdbeobachtung, Navigation und Telekommunikation, Technologien für die Raumfahrt sowie Weltraumwissenschaften und Exploration. Insgesamt steht ein Budget von ca. 13 Mio. EUR zur Verfügung. Jetzt einreichen Hinweis: Bitte lesen Sie vor der Einreichung alle Informationen auf dieser Seite aufmerksam durch. Was wird gefördert? Im Fokus der Förderung stehen F&E-Projekte an der Schnittstelle zwischen Weltraum und Digitalen Technologien, zur Anwendung von Satellitendaten, Produktentwicklung für die Raumfahrt mit Hebelwirkung in die ESA, EU und globale institutionelle und kommerzielle Märkte sowie die Beteiligungen an Weltraummissionen. Wer wird gefördert? Antragsberechtigt sind Universitäten, Forschungseinrichtungen, KMU, Industrieunternehmen, Bedarfsträger und sonstige Organisationen. Wie hoch ist die Förderung? Die Förderhöhe richtet sich nach dem eingereichten Förderinstrument und der Organisationsart zwischen 35-100% der Projektkosten. Was sind die Einreichkriterien? Siehe Ausschreibungs- und Instrumentenleitfäden Wie erfolgt die Einreichung? Die Einreichung erfolgt über das eCall-System der FFG, in dem der Projektinhalt und die –kosten dargestellt werden. Welche Dokumente für die Einreichung erforderlich sein werden, wird im Ausschreibungsleitfaden angeführt. Wann gibt es eine Entscheidung? Die Förderentscheidung ist für April 2027 geplant.
